Referred to the House Committee on Foreign Affairs.

dimensions.assessment: Directly affects the Department of State, the President, and congressional committees receiving or exempted from recurring foreign affairs reports.
dimensions.evidence: To reduce recurring reporting requirements imposed by law on the Department of State.

dimensions.assessment: Streamlines administrative burdens by eliminating certain statutory reports and converting others from semiannual or quarterly to annual schedules.
dimensions.evidence: The President shall not be required to submit to Congress the report described in such subsection.

dimensions.assessment: The source material mentions no federal spending changes, appropriations, or economic impacts beyond minor administrative efficiencies.
Amends numerous past acts, defense authorization acts, and foreign relations statutes by striking subsections and altering reporting timelines across a broad range of foreign policy topics.
dimensions.evidence: Section 5520 of the James M. Inhofe National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023... is amended by striking subsection (b).

dimensions.assessment: Makes permanent statutory repeals and extends or caps modified reporting requirements through specific dates such as December 31, 2030 or 2038.

missing_information: Quantitative estimates of administrative cost savings resulting from reduced reporting
importance_detail.rationale: This bill repeals various recurring reporting requirements for the Department of State and modifies numerous other recurring reports by reducing their frequency or setting expiration dates through December 31, 2030 or 2038.
